children: Kuwait Petroleum Corp has offered 34,000-35,000 metric tons of 93-octane non-oxygenated gasoline in a tender on a free-on-board (FOB) basis from its Mina Al-Ahmadi port, a document reviewed by Reuters showed on Friday.
The cargo is scheduled to load between December 9 and December 10, according to the tender, which closed on Wednesday.
The state-run refiner sold the same grade fuel for late-November loading at a premium of around $180 to $200 per ton to Middle East naphtha quotes, market participants said.
It was KPC's first gasoline offer via a tender after a gap of several months since the war in the Gulf broke out.
Oil companies typically do not comment on tenders.
